analysis.title: GS EUROPEAN EXPRESS: Brokers & Crypto | Halma | Auto1 Group | Knorr Bremse | TMICC | Macro | Global | Corporate Access
key_insights: Binance disclosed a cybersecurity incident on 10/29 affecting ~$6.3bn of assets, the largest crypto cyberattack to date by affected assets. $19.9bn, or 14% of assets on platform, has left Binance since the disclosure.

GS links the Binance incident to a 4% sell-off in total crypto market cap since the day before the hack and sees it as a negative for digital assets coverage. Most impacted are BTGO, COIN and GEMI, and to a lesser extent CRCL, ETOR, GLXY, HOOD and SQN.

Halma: GS reiterates Buy (Conviction List) with 48% upside, arguing the valuation over-discounts Photonics growth concerns. If Photonics revenue went to zero, FY27/28E adj. EPS would fall c.25%/26%, implying 31.8x 12m forward P/E ex-Photonics at 3448p. At a 10Y median P/E of 30.2x the market values Photonics at under 8x.

Auto1 Group: October 2026 high-frequency data shows Autohero average days on website improved to 32 days (vs 37 in Q3), supporting GS's 4Q26 GPU estimate of EUR 2,795 (+2% qoq). 4Q26 units sold run-rate is about 21% yoy. Buy with 72% upside. Q3 results are due Nov 4.
Auto1 key debates: Merchant units sold deceleration in Q3, pace of Autohero refurbishment capacity, sustainability of GPU gains, impact of sustained high oil prices, and appointment of a new CFO.

Knorr Bremse: GS cuts FY27/28E adj. EBIT by 3%/6% after Q3 on weaker RVS orders (second quarter of misses), but stays 5%/6% above Visible Alpha consensus. CVS order recovery continues. Buy, PT cut by 8%, 27% upside.

The Magnum Ice Cream Co (TMICC): Q3 organic growth of +9.6% vs company-compiled consensus +4.6%, with 2-3ppt from European weather that becomes a -70bp headwind in 2027. GS expects 2027 volume growth of +0.1% on +6% raw and packaging inflation and +3.7% pricing, and adj. EBITDA growth of +5.2% vs consensus +6.6%. Sell.

GOAL Kickstart: Global AI-linked stocks sold off last week on AI capex, monetisation and disruption concerns, with Nasdaq down 9% from its October peak and underperforming S&P equal-weight by 12%. S&P 500 Q3 2026 EPS growth is tracking 33% yoy but momentum is slowing. GS stays OW equities for 3m/12m, N bonds and OW cash for 3m, and upgraded bonds to OW for 12m.

Natural gas: TTF fell 9% intraday vs Friday's 104 EUR/MWh close on headlines of a potential diplomatic attempt and more neutral weather models. Risks to 2027 forecasts are skewed to the upside. GS favours hedging a tight European winter via 1Q27 TTF call spreads given the drop in Hormuz LNG flows.

Other headlines: Marvell to acquire Lumentum, Apple F4Q26 EPS beat on iPhone, Mac and gross margins, Alstom profit warnings for FY26/27, Coloplast softer Q4 26 margin implying consensus downgrades, US ISM Manufacturing above expectations, September construction spending well below expectations.
Upcoming this week: US midterm elections, US labour market data, European central bank meetings, inflation and PMIs. GS webinar on US midterms is on Nov 4.

crypto_views: Binance, the largest crypto exchange by volume, disclosed a cyber incident on 10/29 affecting ~$6.3bn of assets, the largest crypto cyberattack to date by affected assets.
$19.9bn, or 14% of assets on platform, has left Binance since the disclosure.
Total crypto market cap is down 4% since the day before the hack, which GS attributes in part to cybersecurity concerns. The prior comparable loss was the $1.5bn Bybit incident in 2025.
GS sees the incident as a negative for digital assets coverage: most impacted BTGO, COIN, GEMI, and less so CRCL, ETOR, GLXY, HOOD, SQN.
